question.problem:
A curve is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x={e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t),\,y={e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t),\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Determine the values of $t$ at which the tangent to the curve is vertical. Do not round the answers.

In **ascending order**, the tangent to the curve is vertical at $t=$
{{field-1}}
and $t=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
The slope $m$ of a tangent line to a curve defined parametrically is given by

$$
m=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

The tangent line is vertical if ${x}^{′}(t)=0$ while ${y}^{′}(t)\ne 0.$

So, we first find the derivatives of $x$ and $y:$

$$
{x}^{′}(t)={e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)),\,{y}^{′}(t)={e}^{t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))
$$

Solving ${x}^{′}(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)) & =0 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) & =0 \\ 0 & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(t) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(t) \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)} & =1 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(t)=1 \\ t & =\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{5\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we note that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={e}^{\frac{\pi }{4}}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})]=\sqrt{2}{e}^{\frac{\pi }{4}}\ne 0, \\ {y}^{′}(\frac{5\pi }{4}) & ={e}^{\frac{5\pi }{4}}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4})]=-\sqrt{2}{e}^{\frac{5\pi }{4}}\ne 0,\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the tangent to the curve is vertical at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $t=\frac{5\pi }{4}.$
